quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: When following other vehicles, what is the minimum safe distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds between your vehicle and the car ahead. In bad weather or at high speeds, increase this distance.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a sharp right turn coming up on the road.

questions.question: When can you legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right of a vehicle turning left if there is an available passing lane. You can also pass on the right on multilane roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in foggy weather?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. High beams reflect off fog and rain back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer has less effect than wine.
Wine has less effect than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks have the most effect.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol hurts your reflexes and judgment. The type does not matter—only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.explanation: Slow down when the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions unsafe. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you follow the speed limit.

questions.question: When can roads become very slick?

options.text: When the temperature is below freezing.

questions.explanation: Roads are slick when it first rains because water mixes with oil on the road surface, making it greasy. Roads are also slick when the temperature is below freezing because moisture turns to ice.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection where you arrived at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: If your power steering stops working, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: If power steering stops working, you will need to use more force to steer. Reduce speed and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no traffic crossing.
Keep driving; you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Treat them like stop signs and come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No more dangerous than normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely:
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog. This person is blind.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should start slowing down:

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Slow down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians by using turn signals, brake lights, and your horn when needed.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Just as safe as driving during the day.

questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see in the dark. Other drivers' headlights can temporarily blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Follow what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Slow down and drive with caution when a crossing guard, sign, or law enforcement officer tells you to. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at:
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: You may carefully continue through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when a yellow light appears, you may carefully continue through the intersection.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: As more drivers use the roads, road rage becomes more common. To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards. This sign warns you to drive carefully when the road is wet because it may be slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: Which of the following does not happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You become calmer and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You become calmer and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, makes it harder to see clearly, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your recovery from headlight glare, and often reduces your caution and makes you take more risks.

questions.question: What can help drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.

questions.explanation: Every sudden stop wastes fuel because you must speed up again. If you look ahead, you can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This saves fuel.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: He or she is a police officer.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to prevent injury.

questions.question: After stopping at a stop sign, what should you do before entering the intersection?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to check for any vehicles you might have missed.

questions.question: Who has the right-of-way when you are turning left?

options.text: Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: You must yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians already in the intersection, and other drivers already in the intersection when turning left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the road ahead has curves. Slow down and adjust your speed.

questions.question: Which traffic light tells you to slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be cautious, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels go off the road?

options.text: Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the gas pedal, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Take your foot off the gas and slow down. Keep both hands on the wheel and steer gently back onto the road. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: Where should you look to reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: At the center of the road
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Look at the right edge of the road instead. This prevents the glare from blinding you.

questions.question: What is true about emergency vehicles?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights. Follow their loudspeaker instructions. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so proceed only when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if you are driving slowly and cars are backing up behind you?

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let the other cars pass your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. Pull off the road on the right side and let traffic pass. Only drive slowly when conditions require it.
